title: Dashboard panel cost amortization and telemetry squeeze
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a practical, SLO-aligned approach to budget telemetry costs at the dashboard panel level and to reduce query & trace sprawl while preserving operator effectiveness. It pairs a per-panel query-cost amortization model with an SLO-tier driven trace-sampling policy and a lightweight operator onboarding checklist to ensure changes are maintainable.

Context and problem statement:
- Observability cost is dominated by frequent, high-cardinality dashboard panels and expensive trace query patterns (session reconstructions, large GROUP BYs).
- Dashboards evolved organically: many panels run heavy queries by default, and operators rely on them during incidents.
- We need a model that: (a) reduces tooling bill, (b) maintains signal for investigations, (c) makes trade-offs visible to panel owners and product teams.

Goals:
1) Establish a repeatable method to estimate and assign a monthly telemetry budget to dashboard panels.
2) Reduce snapshot/query cost by 30% in 3 months without materially increasing MTTR.
3) Tie trace sampling and retention decisions to SLO tiers and operator playbooks.
4) Provide an onboarding micro-checklist so new operators can make safe panel edits.

Key definitions (for this doc):
- Query cost: estimated cloud/metrics vendor compute cost driven by query frequency, time range, and cardinality.
- Panel weight: relative cost factor for a panel = (query_frequency_per_hour) * (avg_time_range_hours) * (cardinality_factor).
- Amortized panel budget: monthly $ budget = panel_weight * vendor_unit_cost * fudge_factor(1.15).
- Incident-critical panel: a panel used in >=2 runbooks or called out in the oncall handbook.
- SLO tiers: Critical (P0/P1 services), Important (P2), Low-impact (P3 and investigative).

Proposed telemetry budgeting model (panel-level):
1) Compute panel_weight for every active panel (run weekly inventory job). Use simple heuristics: cardinality_factor = 1 for low-cardinality queries, 3 for medium, 6 for high (high = GROUP BY tenant_id or similar).
2) Convert weight -> monthly budget using vendor_unit_cost (we get from billing pipeline). Tag panels with estimated monthly cost.
3) Publish costs to panel metadata in dashboard platform and to the dashboard catalog page.
4) Enforce soft quotas: when a panel’s estimated cost > 2x historical owner budget, create an automated review ticket and add a banner suggesting optimizations.

Optimization patterns (for owners to apply):
- Narrow default time ranges (e.g., recent 6h by default with quick toggle for 24h).
- Replace wide GROUP BYs with sampled rollups or pre-aggregated materialized views for common slices (tenant, model_id).
- Move expensive ad-hoc queries into a “diagnostic” dashboard tagged investigational with lower query frequency and higher latency tolerance.
- Cache panel responses for highly repeated queries (short TTL 30–90s) where freshness tolerances allow.

Trace sampling tied to SLO tiers (practical heuristics):
- High-tier services (Critical): sample 100% of error traces; sample 20–40% of success traces focused on high-latency percentiles (>95p). Keep full traces for canary traffic and small request subsets.
- Important-tier services: sample 100% of anomalies (error or latency > 99p), sample 10% of success traces.
- Low-impact services: sample errors at 50% and success at 1–2% or rely on span-level counters only.
- Implement deterministic sampling keys for multi-tenant requests (hash tenant_id mod N) so operators can request targeted replays by flipping sampling flags for a tenant.
- Always capture minimal span breadcrumbs for all requests for quick path reconstruction (span_id, service, op, duration, sampled_flag) kept for 7–30 days depending on tier.

Panel prioritization rubric (score 0–100):
- Operator impact (30): referenced in runbooks or oncall pages (yes=30/no=0).
- SLO relevance (25): directly maps to a customer-facing SLO (full=25, partial=12, none=0).
- Query cost (20): inverse scoring so expensive panels get lower score.
- Investigation utility (15): historically helpful in incidents (based on incident-runbook citations).
- Owner maturity (10): team has an agreed owner and contact.
Panels with score <45 -> candidate for optimization or deprecation. 45–70 -> review for cost-savings. >70 -> exempt from automated throttles but still subject to annual review.

Example rework plan (three sample panels):
1) "Per-tenant latency waterfall" (high card, heavy GROUP BY):
   - Action: Replace with pre-aggregated 5m buckets, move original to diagnostic dashboard.
   - Expected cost delta: -65%
   - Owner: Mateo Alvarez
2) "Global token spend rolling 7d" (low-card, but 1h refresh):
   - Action: Increase refresh to 4h, add cache, keep 1h option behind a quick-toggle for operators.
   - Expected cost delta: -70%
   - Owner: Jordan Ellis
3) "Session reconstruction live view" (trace-heavy):
   - Action: Keep breadcrumbs live; full session reconstruction behind a gated button that triggers on-demand sampling.
   - Expected cost delta: -40% recurring
   - Owner: Hannah Cho

Operator onboarding micro-checklist (for small edits):
- Step 1: Open catalog entry for panel and confirm owner email and tags.
- Step 2: Run the cost estimator script (link in the catalog) and record current panel_weight in the edit.
- Step 3: If estimated monthly cost > $X threshold (TBD), open a review ticket before changing refresh rates or cardinality.
- Step 4: If making a query heavier or adding GROUP BY, add a compact comment describing expected usage patterns and a rollback plan.
- Step 5: After change, monitor panel query volume for 48–72 hours and document outcome in ticket.

Migration timeline (90-day plan):
- Week 0–2: Run inventory job and publish per-panel estimated costs.
- Week 3–6: Kick off owners review for top 200 costliest panels; apply quick wins (range, refresh changes).
- Week 7–12: Implement trace-sampling tiers and deterministic sampling keys for tenants.
- Week 13–14: Audit impact, adjust thresholds, prepare roll-forward plan for next quarter.

Open questions and risks:
- Measurement accuracy: vendor cost attribution may lag; we need continuous reconciliation to avoid chasing noise.
- Owner bandwidth: teams may lack bandwidth to rework panels; consider a small observability SWAT to handle the heaviest panels.
- MTTR impact: risk that over-aggressive sampling increases time to resolve novel incidents. We'll guard with conservative thresholds on critical services and runback tests.

Action items (owner -> short due dates):
- Priya: schedule inventory job + add per-panel metadata (due 2024-09-24).
- Mateo: prototype pre-aggregation pipeline for tenant-latency (due 2024-10-08).
- Jordan: add cost estimator button to dashboard catalog (due 2024-10-01).
- Ops lead: recruit 1 FTE for observability SWAT (proposal by 2024-10-15).

Appendix: quick scripts and queries (links)
- Cost estimator notebook: https://git.internal.redwood/observability/cost-estimator
- Sampling config repo: https://git.internal.redwood/trace/sampling-config
- Dashboard catalog page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Dashboard+Catalog

Notes to reviewers: looking for feedback on cardinality_factor multipliers and a proposed threshold for the ‘expensive panel’ ticketing rule. If we agree on multipliers, I will run a pilot on the top 100 panels and report back with cost delta estimates.
